corrected_verdict: KNOWN_TECHNIQUE (math core classical). The equal-share case is classical (Alon-Roichman Prop 3; Friedman-Murty-Tillich 2006). The weighted l_{1/s}-budget version for all K=o(log p) also follows in a few lines from Dirichlet/Minkowski pigeonhole with frequency-dependent radii rho_j=(c/y_j)^{1/2}. That gives m(y) <= 8 pi^2 K^{1-s} p^{-2/K} = 8 pi^2 (ln p)^{1-s} x^{s-1} e^{-2x} for K <= 2 ln p/s, which is sharper than the paper's eq:Kbound. Only the transfer to network margins with interference allowed (h <= ||A||_{1/s} m(A/||A||)) is paper-specific.
issues:
1) The checker's key novelty claim is false. It says that simultaneous Dirichlet approximation alone only reaches K=O(log p/log log p) and that the positive-Fourier inequality (eq:posfourier) is needed for all K=o(log p). That holds only when every frequency gets the same radius. Weighted pigeonhole (Minkowski's linear forms theorem / multi-radius Bohr-set size bound) gives the full weighted corollary:
- Set rho_j=(c/y_j)^{1/2} and N_j=ceil(1/rho_j)<=2/rho_j. By AM-GM on the budget, prod y_j<=K^{-sK}. The pigeonhole then gives delta!=0 with ||j delta/p||<=rho_j once c~4K^{-s}p^{-2/K}.
- So F(delta)<=2 pi^2 K c. The ratio to Gamma_s is O(x^{s-1}e^{-2x}), against the paper's x^s e^{-sx/(6+s)}.
- Checked numerically on p up to 100003, s in {1.25,1.5,2,3}, K<=6, random shares: max m/bound = 0.25, never violated.
- The same pigeonhole plus the tail bound y_(i)<=i^{-s} also yields Gamma_s=O((ln p)^{1-s}) in thm:scaling.
